A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TopoTune/GCCN work. All 29 pages, including Appendices A–I, are available; text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of equations, figures, tables, and the algorithm.

before.justification: v4 reports original GCCN benchmark experiments in Section 6 and additional dataset and model evaluations in Appendix H.

after.justification: v5 retains the original GCCN experiments in Section 6 and Appendix H, including classification and regression results.

M1.justification: The Hasse-graph expansion, per-rank neighborhoods, neighborhood models, and aggregation procedure are unchanged in Section 4, Equations 6–8, and Appendix D's Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Both retain the eight main benchmarks and four larger heterophilic datasets in Appendix H.1, with the same graph-level and node-level tasks and topological domains.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same GNN, CCNN, and hypergraph comparators, including SCCN/CWN in Table 2 and the Appendix H comparisons. Table 6 changes baseline timings without changing comparator membership.

E3.justification: Splits, metrics, hyperparameter grids, and training procedures remain unchanged in Section 6 and Appendix E. Appendix G still specifies timing on one NVIDIA A30 GPU; no revised timing protocol is documented.

E4.justification: The graph-expansion comparisons, neighborhood/model analyses, and performance-versus-size analyses in Figures 5 and 10 are retained. Table 6 revises benchmark timings without adding an ablation or a new analytical question.

E5.justification: The five-seed/split statements and uncertainty-reporting conventions are unchanged. Table 6 replaces numerical estimates and their accompanying ± values without changing the reported statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Table 6 revises all three CCNN baseline timing rows. For example, cellular MUTAG changes from 100 ± 23 to 19.8 ± 6 seconds, and simplicial ZINC from 178 ± 86 to 1403 ± 605 seconds. This alters runtime comparisons, but GCCN timings, Table 7, and predictive results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Propositions 4.1–4.3, Appendix B proofs and counterexample, and Appendix C complexity derivations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The rewritten abstract retains the same contributions: systematic construction of GCCNs, generalization of CCNNs, competitive performance with reduced model complexity, and TopoTune software. The introduction's contribution list and conclusion are unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 6.2 retains its interpretation of runtime differences and on-the-fly graph-expansion overhead despite the revised timings. The lifting and memory limitations in Appendix E.2 and future-work discussion are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix G revises the reported training costs of the CCNN baselines in Table 6. Implementation instructions, hyperparameters, hardware descriptions, and code-access information remain unchanged; no underlying implementation change is documented.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to earlier graph-expansion methods, CCNNs, TopoX, and TopoBench are unchanged. Citations crossing the page 1–2 boundary are relocated by reflow, not added or removed.

P1.justification: The opening portion of the abstract is rewritten more concisely, and v5 adds an ICML/PMLR publication notice. The remaining narrative and section/appendix organization are essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: The shortened abstract and added publication footer reflow the opening pages. Figures and the algorithm are identical, while table structures, captions, and appendix placement remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The abstract is more concise, but Table 6's unexplained timing revisions materially alter efficiency comparisons: the cellular MUTAG baseline becomes faster rather than slower than every listed GCCN. v5 documents neither a protocol change nor why these estimates were replaced. Their reliability benefit cannot be established from the PDFs, leaving the overall quality direction uncertain.
